guide:
# LaRuche 2048: read before playing
## Objective
2048 is a one-player sliding-tile puzzle, not an adversarial game. The primary objective is to create a tile of value 2048. Only after the human explicitly chooses Continue should play pursue larger tiles and a higher score. A high score alone does not mean 2048 was reached. There is no second player or alternating color.
Use this installed App (dev.laruche.2048), not an external 2048 website or newly generated HTML.

## Board and scoring
board is an array of exactly 16 nonnegative integers, row-major on a 4x4 grid. index=row*4+column, row 0 top, column 0 left. Indexes 0..3 are the first row and 12..15 the last. Zero means empty; occupied cells contain powers of two starting at 2.
The initial board has two random tiles. score counts points earned by merges, best is the recorded high score, moves counts successful directions, revision is an opaque optimistic-concurrency value. Do not derive the revision from score or move count.

## A complete move
Only four directions exist: left, right, up, down. One move slides ALL tiles as far as possible in that direction, not a chosen tile. Ignore zero gaps while sliding. Adjacent equal tiles merge into their doubled value, and each tile can participate in at most one merge during that move. A freshly merged tile cannot merge again until a later move.
Examples BEFORE the new random tile appears:
- [2,0,2,0] left -> [4,0,0,0], score +4.
- [2,2,2,2] left -> [4,4,0,0], score +8, NOT [8,0,0,0].
- [2,2,4,0] left -> [4,4,0,0], score +4, NOT [8,0,0,0].
- [2,2,2,0] right -> [0,0,2,4], score +4.
- [2,4,8,16] left does not change that row and earns no points.
After a direction that changes the board, ONE empty square receives a random tile: 2 with probability 90%, 4 with probability 10%. The server/App reports the actual result; never invent the random square or claim a deterministic future board.
An unchanged direction is not a legal turn and must not be sent. A direction may be legal without making a merge, because moving into empty space is useful. Use the returned legalMoves rather than guessing.

## Reading victory, pause and defeat
game.state returns goal, rules, board, score, best, moves, revision, won, keepPlaying, needsContinue, over, waitingFor and legalMoves.
- won=true means a 2048-or-larger tile exists. It stays true during extended play.
- needsContinue=true means the victory overlay is waiting for the HUMAN to press Continue. legalMoves is empty then, even if the board could otherwise move. Stop and congratulate the human; do not mistake this for a loss or reset the board.
- keepPlaying=true means Continue was chosen; larger tiles may be pursued.
- over=true means no direction can change the board. A full board is not automatically over: equal adjacent neighbors can still merge.
- waitingFor is move, humanContinue or finished. Only move allows an agent action.
If no legal move exists, report the actual reason using these fields. Do not repeatedly call the LLM, move, undo or restart on its own.

## Exact agent workflow
1. app_list -> app_guide for dev.laruche.2048 -> app_open its game view -> app_wait until ready. Use the selected instanceId when several views are connected.
2. Call game.state with {}. Read the goal/rules and current legalMoves. Respect any new instructions from the human.
3. If waitingFor=move, choose ONE direction appearing in legalMoves.
4. Call game.move with ONLY {direction: chosenDirection, revision: currentRevision}.
5. Read its returned actual board, score and terminal status. Replan from this state after every move; randomness and human input invalidate cached boards.
For host tools: app_call({appId:"dev.laruche.2048",instanceId,action:"game.move",arguments:{direction,revision}}).
For the App's agents.act turn: return ONLY {"action":"game.move","arguments":{"direction":"CHOSEN_LEGAL_DIRECTION","revision":CURRENT_REVISION}}, replacing the placeholders with actual state values. No Markdown fence, commentary, board or invented arguments.

## Planning suggestions, not additional rules
Prefer keeping empty squares and maintaining a stable corner for the largest tile, with large values arranged monotonically along an edge. Try not to isolate small tiles behind large ones. Compare the allowed moves and their possible random outcomes. Merging immediately is not always better than preserving space; avoid a rigid direction pattern when it would trap the board.
Only legalMoves defines what can be played, not these heuristics. Do not fabricate rollouts, scores or guarantees. You may reason about possible outcomes, but the next observed state is the truth.

## Safety and recovery
Stale revision: reread game.state, then choose again. Illegal move: inspect legalMoves and waitingFor; do not spam the rejected direction. Permission denied: ask for native App action permission, never bypass it with a shell, DOM injection or another website. Loading: app_wait. Disconnected: open the view again and wait.
Never automatically retry a timed-out mutation, as it may have executed. First inspect the actual state.
game.new is a separate destructive action replacing the board (best score retained). It needs both its own permission and an explicit user request for a new game. Do not use it to raise your success rate, escape a loss, clear the victory overlay or handle an error.
The human can play, undo or restart between your actions. The latest revision must always be respected. Auto mode schedules one model turn at a time; Pause lets the current turn finish and cancels subsequent scheduled turns.
The latest board is saved through private App storage, not browser localStorage. Wait for Synced before closing. Independent windows do not synchronize live; use one playing instance.

actions.description: Read the board, score, legal moves and revision.

actions.name: game.move
actions.description: Play one legal direction at the exact current revision.
